steps.name: Pure summary: per-search found, other, on-target and unique over two scopes
criteria: The cohort gives each saved search its found, other, on-target and unique figures, ordered by found descending then search ascending by code unit, with the unparsed row and the total, and the cohort and spread-cohort figures equal what the independent oracle derives from the DESIGN rules

An advert found by two searches counts under both for found and on-target and under neither for unique; an advert resent by one search counts once; a repost under a new advert id counts twice; the total counts distinct adverts, not the sum over searches
The family counted is the advert's first-sighting title, in both directions (a later title never changes it), under every search that found the advert and in every scope

The unparsed bucket is its own row with unique shown as not applicable, is never a rival search in anyone's unique reckoning, treats an empty term as no term, and is absent from a scope where every sighting named its search

A block is null when its scope holds fewer than two named searches; an empty list of sightings gives no block at all and does not throw; the summary never changes the sightings or adverts it is handed

The recent block counts the 28 calendar dates ending at the latest sighting date, inclusive at both ends (27th day before counts, 28th does not), is omitted when the cache fits inside 28 dates (28 fit, 29 do not) or holds fewer than two named searches in the window, never reads the clock, and judges family and unique inside the scope counted

An advert first seen before the window and resent inside it counts under the resending search with its original family; a search that appears only inside the window has the same found in both blocks; a sighting with an unreadable date counts all-time only, is outside the window and never throws

The properties hold over generated sightings: other plus on-target is found for every row and the total; unique is at most on-target is at most found; found sums to the distinct (advert, search) pairs; the order is found descending then search ascending; a block is present exactly when two or more named searches exist; unique means sent by that search alone and on-target; unparsed sightings never change a named row; recent is at most all-time; the recent block ends at the latest date and exists only beyond 28 dates; shifting every date by the same days changes no figure; every figure equals the oracle; shuffling the sightings changes nothing; any input including null terms, unreadable dates and odd titles gives a summary and never throws

src/core/search-yield.mjs imports only core modules, declares no class, mutates no input and uses no node: builtin; the exported constant names and values are unchanged; npm run check:arch stays green

steps.implementation_notes: Contract shape: pure-function (return-only); universe = the returned { allTime, recent } value, the inputs are never touched. Implement summariseSearchYield(sightings, adverts) in src/core/search-yield.mjs to the ratified shape (feature-delta Pre-requisites and Decisions Pinned by Tests, 2026-10-05): { allTime, recent }, each a block or null; block = { scope, endDate (recent only, YYYY-MM-DD), searches: [{ search, found, other, onTarget, unique }] (every named search, the cap is the formatter's), unparsed: { found, other, onTarget } | null, total: { found, other, onTarget } }. Family = classifyRoleFamily of the ADVERT's (collapsed row's) title, imported from role-families.mjs (core to core); never a sighting's title. The omission rules live here (null block), not in the formatter. formatSearchYield keeps its scaffold throw until step 01-02, and __SCAFFOLD__ stays until step 03-01. SIZING NOTE: 39 scenarios and 9 behaviour groups, but all run against one function over one in-memory structure (scope selection, per-search sets, family lookup, window arithmetic), so a half cannot go green alone and the step is NOT split. The crafter commits in slices, each leaving npm test green: (1) the import-purity guard (green today), all-time figures, ordering, overlap, resend, repost and first-sighting family with the oracle scenario; (2) the unparsed row and the omission rules; (3) the recent window and unreadable dates; (4) the properties. Window arithmetic uses date-string or epoch-day arithmetic without Date.now or new Date() with no argument and no node: import; the properties include one that translates all dates by a constant. Enabling mechanism (crafter-owned; recommended): change scenario( to it( per scenario, in the same commit as the code that makes it pass, so every commit leaves npm test green. Per-file removal of the skip switch is not workable because the summary and properties files are each shared by several steps, so keep the red-gate import in every file until step 03-01. steps.name: Pure formatter: headings, fixed widths, truncation, cap line and half-up percentages
criteria: A block prints its heading, the column header, one row per search, the unparsed row and the total in the pinned fixed widths: label left-aligned in 40, found right-aligned in 5, other as 'n (p%)' in 9, on-target in 9, unique in 6, two spaces between columns; the recent heading names the end date and the window
Headings are verbatim: 'harvest build: search yield, all cached alerts (distinct adverts per saved search)' and 'harvest build: search yield, last 28 days to <date>'
A label of exactly 40 characters is printed whole; one of 41 is cut to its first 37 characters then '...'

Exactly twenty named searches print no more-line; twenty-one print one 'more search(es) not shown' line, twenty-three print three; the unparsed and total rows follow the cap line and the total still counts every advert
The unparsed row is absent when every sighting named its search; nothing is printed when both blocks are null; a figure wider than its column is printed in full, never cut
Percentages are whole numbers rounded half up: 1 of 8 is 13%, 3 of 8 is 38%, 1 of 3 is 33%, 2 of 3 is 67%, 1 of 6 is 17%, 5 of 6 is 83%, 1 of 200 is 1%; every other is 100% and none other is 0%

The printed lines equal the oracle's for the cohorts and for generated sightings (labels at and beyond 40 characters included); with up to 26 searches at most twenty are listed and the total counts all; every table line has the same width and no label is wider than the column; the share is an integer from 0 to 100
src/core stays pure: no node: imports, no classes, no mutation; npm run check:arch green; every existing test passes unmodified
steps.scenario_name: 21 scenarios: search-yield-summary.test.mjs 16 (the 'formatter prints a block as the stderr lines the DESIGN pins' describe, every scenario: cohort lines 1, spread cohort both blocks 1, 40 and 41 character labels 1, cap at 20, 21 and 23 1, unparsed and total after the cap line 1, nothing printed when both blocks are null 1, wider figure 1, 100% and 0% 1, seven rounding cases 7, printed lines equal the oracle's 1); search-yield-properties.test.mjs 5 (the 'printed lines follow the DESIGN rule' describe: lines equal the oracle 1, cap with up to 26 searches 1, P7 share 1, all-other 100% and none 0% 1, every line the same width 1)
steps.implementation_notes: Contract shape: pure-function (return-only): formatSearchYield(searchYield) returns an array of stderr lines, empty when both blocks are null; it performs no I/O and decides no omission (the summary already nulled those blocks). Reads the exported constants for window days, label width, row cap and the two row labels; do not repeat their values as literals. Blocks print all-time first. The unparsed row prints only when its found is at least 1; the total row always prints; both show the pinned dash in the unique column. Sort order is the summary's, not re-derived. Use padStart and padEnd; no table library (Cognitive Load Tax, feature-delta Technology Choices). Percent is Math.round(100 * other / found) (half up; found is at least 1 for every listed row). SIZING NOTE: 21 scenarios, 8+ behaviours, but one function and one row-rendering routine; seven of the 21 are the same rounding scenario over seven inputs. The crafter commits in slices: (1) heading, header and rows in fixed widths for the cohort and spread cohort; (2) truncation and the cap line with the rows that follow it; (3) the rounding cases and wide figures; (4) the properties. After this step no scaffold throw remains in search-yield.mjs, but __SCAFFOLD__ is deleted in 03-01 with the rest of the scaffold. steps.name: The CLI prints the search yield on stderr at the merge, Sheets and dry-run sites
criteria: WALKING SKELETON: build --target sheets against a Sheet holding only its headers, over a synthetic two-month cache of three overlapping searches, prints on stderr the all-time block and the last-28-days block with found, other, on-target and unique per search

build --out <f> --merge <f> prints the all-time block on stderr after the change summary and the role-family view, in the pinned lines, and a second build or merge prints the same lines and changes nothing

--dry-run on either target, with or without --merge, prints the same lines the build then prints, on stderr after its own plan summary and role-family view; the workspace is byte-identical, the Sheets fake records no write request, and a preview with no tracker prints the yield and creates no file
The yield never appears on stdout and never in the --report file; an empty report still means nothing changed when the yield is printed against a tracker or Sheet that already holds everything
Creating a new workbook (build --out <new>) and the --in rebuild print no yield; a merge into the result then does

The yield does not depend on what the tracker or Sheet holds (an empty one and a filled, extended one give the same lines); the tracker is cell for cell unchanged, no yield tab, column or cell is added, and every Sheets request that wrote is inside the four allowed kinds and touches only declared columns; a second Sheets build sends no further data batch

Nothing prints when there is nothing to compare: one named search, only unparsed alerts, or an empty cache (the build still refuses as it always did); once a second search or alerts arrive, the next build prints

The recent block ends at the latest sighting date, not the clock (the same cache merged on two different days gives the same lines); a stale cache shows its own end date; a cache within 28 dates prints only the all-time block and one date more adds the recent block

found agrees with the Sources tab Jobs Found and the total with the Jobs tab; overlap, resends, reposts, retitled adverts, the unparsed row and blank terms read as the pure scenarios say; labels over 40 characters are cut and 23 searches print 20 plus a 'more not shown' line while the tracker lists all 23, and exactly 20 print no such line
build still accepts exactly its five options: --since is refused as an unknown option, nothing is written, and src/core/cli-options.mjs is unchanged
src/core stays pure; npm run check:arch green; every existing test passes unmodified

steps.implementation_notes: Contract shape: bounded-change for the merge and Sheets scenarios (the yield adds no cell, column or tab: universe = tracker, Sheet, workspace and stderr); unbounded-preservation for the four xlsx and three Sheets dry-run scenarios (nothing written, no write capability constructed). The shell change is imperative and effect-isolated (feature-delta Component Decomposition): add printSearchYield(model) in src/cli/harvest.mjs, which writes one console.error per line of formatSearchYield(model.searchYield), and call it directly after printTuningView at the three sites: reportDryRun (gains the model argument; its caller at the sheet-state dry-run already holds the model), runMergeBuild, and runSheetsBuild. No stdout write, no report writer change, no new option (an entry in cli-options would break the unknown-option guard and needs a decision), no change to the create and --in paths. No new capability or adapter is constructed. SIZING NOTE: 42 scenarios, 8+ behaviours, but one print function at three call sites, with every behaviour beyond presence already pinned by the pure steps; the figures and the lines come from steps 01-01 to 02-01, so the new code is about one function and three calls. Enable the Sheets walking skeleton first (the first scenario that exercises the whole path), then the merge describe, then the dry-run describe, then the create and rebuild silence and the option guard, then the agreement, nothing-to-compare, recent-block and bounded-output scenarios, then the remaining Sheets scenarios. Commit in two slices, each leaving npm test green: (1) the print function with the Sheets build and the merge site (walking skeleton, merge, silence); (2) the dry-run site, with reportDryRun gaining the model, and the remaining scenarios. The ten Sheets scenarios use the existing loopback sheets-fake and the temp-HOME credentials; the fake models no request-count ceiling and this feature changes no request, so the live Sheets behaviour of a build that sends no data batch is not proven here. Where a scenario fails for a reason other than a missing print (for example the cache reader, merge planning or an adapter), it is a finding: report it before editing any module outside src/cli/harvest.mjs. The Y2 xlsx dry-run assertion is a byte-identical workspace because only the Sheets fake keeps a request log.
